posts.hook: We manage 20 flats in London. Here's what that actually looks like at 7am.
posts.concept: Founder-led intro. Fast cuts: keys, a turnover in progress, a tube platform, a made bed, a guest arriving. Ends on your face saying the one sentence of what Seeker Estates is.
posts.why: Introduce the brand in plain English. No corporate language. State the number (20), the city, and who you serve. Pin this post.
posts.cta: Follow for London stays + what's actually on this week
posts.assets: Founder piece-to-camera (15s), 6 B-roll clips from any property, 1 street/tube clip

posts.hook: The Bayeux Tapestry is in London for the first time in 950 years.
posts.concept: Opened at the British Museum yesterday (10 Sep 2026) — the biggest UK cultural loan in a generation, running to 11 Jul 2027. Six slides: what it is, why it matters, how to book, nearest tube, what else is walkable, where to stay nearby.
posts.why: This is a genuine news peg on day two of the account. Lead with the fact, not with yourself. Mention your Bloomsbury/Zone 1 stock only on the final slide.
posts.cta: Save this for when you book
posts.assets: Stock/press images of the British Museum exterior, 1 clip of Great Russell St, map graphic

posts.hook: London Design Festival started today and most of it is free.
posts.concept: Rapid list of 5 free LDF things across different districts (Brompton, Shoreditch, Bankside, Mayfair, King's Cross) with the tube stop stamped on each. Runs 12-20 Sep.
posts.why: Note it's dispersed across the city — which quietly justifies staying outside Zone 1. Don't say that out loud yet; the geography does the work.
posts.assets: 5 short clips or stock of each district, on-screen text overlays

posts.hook: This is the busiest week in London until Christmas. Here's what's actually happening.
posts.concept: Weekly anchor format #1. Fashion Week (17-21), Design Festival (to 20), Open House London. Three events, three tube stops, one line each. Establish this Monday slot as a habit.
posts.why: Set the template: 'LONDON THIS WEEK' as a fixed on-screen title card. Same music bed, same font, every Monday. This becomes the show people come back for.
posts.assets: Title card graphic, 3 event clips/stock, ambient London audio

posts.hook: £240 a night in London. Hotel room vs our flat. Same postcode.
posts.concept: Side-by-side comparison carousel. Slides alternate: hotel room photo / your flat photo, with the same annotation categories — space, kitchen, laundry, desk, cost of breakfast for 4.
posts.why: Be scrupulously fair. Use a real hotel price you can screenshot, and your real rate. Do not name the hotel. The honesty is the persuasion.
posts.cta: Link in bio for direct rates
posts.assets: Full photo set of ONE flagship flat + screenshot of a comparable hotel listing

posts.hook: Section 21 is gone. Here's what that actually means if you own a London flat.
posts.concept: The Renters' Rights Act 2025 commenced 1 May 2026: all ASTs periodic, Ground 1A (sale) needs 4 months' notice and is barred for 12 months, Ground 8 arrears threshold now 3 months. Explain it straight, no pitch.
posts.why: LANDLORD DAY format #1. Pure education, zero selling. The CTA is a save, not an enquiry. Trust is built by being the account that explained it first. FACT-CHECK every clause before posting.
posts.cta: Save this. Send it to a landlord who hasn't read it.
posts.assets: Text-on-screen graphics only — no footage needed

posts.hook: Nobody photographs this part of a short-let. So we did.
posts.concept: The turnover. Real footage, unglamorous: stripping beds, the laundry run, checking under the sofa, the linen count, restocking. Ends on the finished room. No music-video gloss.
posts.why: PROOF DAY format #1. The category's trust problem is 'is this place actually clean and actually real'. Showing the boring work answers it better than any five-star screenshot.
posts.cta: This happens between every single guest.
posts.assets: Film one full turnover on a phone — 15 clips, 3-5s each

posts.hook: Open House weekend: 8 London buildings you can walk into for free this weekend, today only.
posts.concept: Fast-cut list with addresses and nearest tube. Urgency is real — it's this weekend.
posts.why: Saturday DISCOVER slot. Post by 8am. Time-sensitive content gets shared in group chats, which is the highest-value share there is.
posts.cta: Send this to whoever you're going with
posts.assets: Stock/press images of the buildings, on-screen text

posts.hook: Laver Cup, England v Spain, and the last of Fashion Week. London this week.
posts.concept: Weekly anchor #2. Laver Cup at The O2 25-27 Sep (note: the ATP Finals are in Turin, not London — say so, it's a genuine correction people will thank you for). England v Spain at Wembley Sat 26.
posts.why: The ATP correction is a great engagement hook because half of London gets it wrong. Being right is a personality.
posts.assets: Title card, O2 exterior clip, Wembley clip

posts.hook: You land at Heathrow at 6am and can't check in until 3. Here's the nine-hour plan.
posts.concept: The single most save-worthy post you can make. Luggage storage options with prices, breakfast near the Piccadilly line, a shower option, a free museum that opens at 10, and where to be at 2:45.
posts.why: PRACTICAL slot. This solves a real problem for every long-haul arrival. It will get saved and sent for years. Update the prices annually.
posts.cta: Save this before your next early flight
posts.assets: Heathrow arrivals clip, tube clip, 3 location clips — or good stock

posts.hook: Your flat can legally be short-let for 90 nights a year. Most people find out too late.
posts.concept: The Deregulation Act 2015 s.44 rule — and the part almost nobody mentions: there are TWO conditions, 90 nights AND someone liable for council tax. Camden's own May 2026 report found 64% of its 7,516 short-lets exceeded 90 nights in 2025.
posts.why: LANDLORD DAY #2. Not one competitor homepage explains this rule — that is your opening. Being the operator who volunteers the inconvenient regulation is the entire trust play. Add: 'this is general information, not legal advice.'
posts.cta: Save it. Ask us anything in the comments.
posts.assets: Text-on-screen graphics, maybe a Camden street clip

posts.hook: Eleven guests told us the sofa was uncomfortable. Here's what we did.
posts.concept: Show the actual review quotes (anonymised), then the replacement sofa, then the review that came after. A visible feedback loop.
posts.why: PROOF DAY #2. This format is unbeatable because it admits a fault. Nobody expects a company to publish its own bad reviews. Do this every time you fix something.
posts.cta: Tell us what we should fix next 👇
posts.assets: Screenshots of real reviews (anonymised), before/after sofa photos

posts.hook: Where to actually eat around Wembley before kick-off — not the ground.
posts.concept: England v Spain today. 5 spots within 12 minutes' walk of Wembley Park station, with prices. Post at 9am for a 5pm kick-off.
posts.why: Match-day content posted the morning of the match is a share machine. Repeat this format for every big Wembley/Twickenham date in the calendar.
posts.cta: Send this to whoever's got the tickets
posts.assets: 5 food spot clips or stock, Wembley Way clip

posts.hook: ExCeL has three expos this week and the Film Festival starts Thursday.
posts.concept: Weekly anchor #3. Corporate-leaning week: ExCeL cluster, International Security/Cyber Expo, BFI LFF opens 1 Oct.
posts.why: Rotate the weekly anchor's tone with the week's audience — this one skews corporate, so the language is drier and the tube-stop information is the value.
posts.assets: Title card, ExCeL clip, Southbank clip
posts.event: ExCeL expo cluster, BFI LFF opens 1 Oct

posts.hook: Nine minutes from ExCeL. This is the flat, and this is the walk.
posts.concept: Single continuous shot: start at the flat's front door, walk to the station, film the platform, film the ExCeL entrance. One take, sped up, with a timer on screen.
posts.why: The 'timed walk' format is your signature. It proves a claim rather than making one. Do one for every property near a major venue. Enormously reassuring for corporate bookers.
posts.cta: Direct rates in bio — no OTA fee
posts.assets: One continuous walk filmed on a phone gimbal or steady hand

posts.hook: 41% of landlords had a void last year. The average was 66 days.
posts.concept: In London that's roughly £5,100 of nothing. Set against ONS July 2026 average London rent of £2,317/month. The pitch isn't 'earn more' — it's 'earn certainly'.
posts.why: LANDLORD DAY #3. This is the strategic heart of your landlord pitch: London SA gross (~£32.2k/listing per AirDNA Sep 2026) is only ~16% above long-let gross on a much heavier cost base. Do NOT sell a yield multiple. Sell certainty, voids covered, and no arrears. Competitors overclaim; you won't.
posts.assets: Data graphics only

posts.hook: Our cleaners know London better than any guidebook. I asked all six for one spot.
posts.concept: Six people, six recommendations, six neighbourhoods. Faces optional — hands, voices, or text cards work.
posts.why: PROOF DAY #3, doubling as team content. It humanises the operation and produces genuinely good London recommendations. Pay them for their time on camera.
posts.cta: Which one are you trying first?
posts.assets: Six short clips or six text cards + one voiceover

posts.hook: The Film Festival is on. Here are the 8 screenings you can still get into.
posts.concept: BFI LFF runs 1-11 Oct. Practical, current, with prices and venues.
posts.why: Saturday DISCOVER. Time-limited utility content — the kind people screenshot.
posts.cta: Save it, the good ones go fast
posts.assets: Southbank/BFI clips or press stills

posts.hook: NFL at Tottenham twice this month, England play Tuesday, and the Film Festival's still running.
posts.concept: Weekly anchor #4. NFL at Spurs 4 & 11 Oct, England v Czechia 6 Oct, LFF continuing.
posts.why: American visitors book 4-7 nights, not 2 — that's the commercial point behind this week's content. Aim some of it at a US audience explicitly.
posts.assets: Title card, Spurs stadium clip, Wembley clip

posts.hook: American in London for the NFL game? Six things that will confuse you.
posts.concept: Contactless on the tube (no ticket needed), which side to stand on the escalator, tipping, the plug, 'first floor' isn't the ground floor, and why nobody has air conditioning.
posts.why: Written for US visitors, who book longer stays. Funny, useful, and geo-relevant. Could travel well on TikTok.
posts.assets: Tube clips, escalator clip, plug close-up — all easy phone shots

posts.hook: Your lender and your freeholder may both say no. Check before you convert.
posts.concept: Mortgage consent-to-let clauses, leasehold covenants against short-letting (Nemcova and Koumetto both went against the leaseholder), buildings insurance, and whether business rates apply.
posts.why: LANDLORD DAY #4. The 'reasons NOT to do this' post. Counter-intuitively your strongest acquisition content — it filters out landlords who'd become problems and earns the trust of the ones who wouldn't. Always flag: not legal advice.
posts.cta: Not sure where you stand? Ask below.
posts.assets: Text graphics

posts.hook: Four things to check before you pay a deposit on ANY London short-let.
posts.concept: Reverse-image the photos, insist on a video call or a real address, check the listing has a phone number that answers, never pay by bank transfer to a personal account.
posts.why: PROOF DAY #4. You are teaching people how to avoid scams — including, implicitly, how to check YOU. Confidence is the message. Massive save and share potential.
posts.cta: Save this. Send it to whoever books your trips.
posts.assets: Text graphics + one screen recording of a reverse image search

posts.hook: Six London museums that are completely free and never busy on a Saturday morning.
posts.concept: Not the British Museum. Sir John Soane's, the Wellcome Collection, the Hunterian, the Foundling Museum, Leighton House, the Garden Museum.
posts.why: Evergreen DISCOVER content. This is the kind of post that keeps earning reach for months. Build 6-8 of these evergreen pillars.
posts.assets: 6 clips or good stock of each

posts.hook: This is the most expensive week to be in London until Christmas. Here's why.
posts.concept: Weekly anchor #5 and the biggest one. Frieze London + Frieze Masters (14-18, Regent's Park), LFF closing, NFL at Wembley Sunday 18, DTX and New Scientist Live.
posts.why: Peak ADR week of the autumn. Content should NOT discount — it should justify. Talk about what's on, not about price.
posts.assets: Title card, Regent's Park clip, Wembley clip

posts.hook: Frieze without a ticket: 10 free shows on in London this week that are arguably better.
posts.concept: Gallery shows, public installations, the Frieze Sculpture park in Regent's Park (free), plus the commercial galleries in Mayfair that are free and open to anyone.
posts.why: The counter-programming play. Frieze coverage is saturated with the ticketed thing; almost nobody covers the free half. This is where the reach is.
posts.cta: Save this — most run all week
posts.assets: 10 gallery/artwork clips or press images

posts.hook: A £65-per-property national database starts on 15 December. Here's what you have to do.
posts.concept: The national landlord database opens 15 Dec 2026 at £65/property/year. Combine with: licensing is at a record 174 designations covering 28 of 33 London boroughs, and £24.1m of London fines were logged to May 2026.
posts.why: LANDLORD DAY #5. Deadline content with a real date creates urgency without you manufacturing any. VERIFY the date and fee before posting — this is regulatory and must be right.
posts.assets: Calendar graphic, text overlays

posts.hook: Every review we got in September. Including the three-star.
posts.concept: Screen-record scrolling through the month's reviews at real speed — the good, the middling, the critical. Then respond on camera to the least flattering one.
posts.why: PROOF DAY #5. Make this a monthly format on the 15th. Publishing the three-star is the whole point; anyone can screenshot a five-star.
posts.assets: Screen recording of reviews + 20s piece-to-camera

posts.hook: Four London flats, four price points, one video. Which one's your trip?
posts.concept: Rapid tour: 30s split four ways. Studio → one-bed → two-bed → the big one. Nightly rate stamped on each.
posts.why: The 'pick one' format drives comments, which drives reach. Rotate the four properties every time you run it so it never repeats.
posts.assets: Photo/video sets for 4 different properties

posts.why: SOFT WEEK STRATEGY: this is a week the content calendar exists to fix. Lean into value and emptiness, not events. 'London is cheap and quiet this week' is a real, true, appealing message.

posts.event: Diwali on the Square, soft week

posts.why: Direct-response content for a soft week. This is where discounting is correct — you're filling an air pocket, not devaluing peak.
posts.cta: Link in bio — this week only

posts.hook: Rent-to-rent just got dangerous. Rent repayment orders now reach the superior landlord.

posts.why: LANDLORD DAY #6. This is the most commercially useful post in the landlord track: it makes cowboy R2R operators radioactive and positions a compliant management company as the safe option. Be precise and cite the Act.

posts.assets: Text graphics

posts.hook: Why we started this, and the flat that nearly ended it.

posts.why: HUMAN slot. Run one of these a month. People book from people. The failure is the interesting part — don't sand it off.
posts.assets: Founder piece-to-camera, photos of the first property

posts.hook: Half term starts Monday. Eleven free things to do with kids in London.
posts.concept: Autumn half term is 26-30 Oct. Free, indoor-heavy (it's late October), spread across zones, with tube stops.

posts.why: The single strongest value argument you have against hotels for families. Use real, checkable numbers.

posts.why: LANDLORD DAY #7. Correcting a live piece of industry misinformation is high-authority content. It also inoculates your prospects against competitors' pitches. Flag: not tax advice, speak to your accountant.

posts.hook: 24 nights of darts at Ally Pally. Here's what's within 20 minutes.
posts.concept: Journey times from your N/NE properties to Alexandra Palace. Timed walk format if you have stock up there.
posts.why: Match your stock to the event. If you have nothing in N London, make this a 'how to get there from anywhere' post instead — usefulness still earns reach.
posts.assets: N London property photos + journey graphics

posts.hook: Everything that changed for London landlords in 2026, in ninety seconds.
posts.concept: The year in review: RRA commencement 1 May, Section 21 gone, RRO reach extended, the database from 15 Dec, licensing at 174 designations, FHL relief gone, the STL register due March 2027.
posts.why: LANDLORD DAY #13. The year-end summary is the most saveable and shareable landlord post you'll make, and it doubles as a portfolio piece proving you know this market.
posts.cta: Save this and read it twice.
posts.assets: Timeline graphic

posts.hook: Ninety days ago this account had no followers. Here's every number.
posts.concept: Full transparency: reach, followers, enquiries, bookings attributed, landlord conversations. Whatever the numbers are.
posts.why: PROOF DAY #13 and the account's 90-day mark. Publishing your real numbers — good or bad — is the highest-trust content that exists, and it sets up the next quarter.
posts.assets: Screen recordings of analytics + piece-to-camera

posts.hook: London between Christmas and New Year: what's actually open.
posts.concept: The genuinely useful dead-zone guide. What's open on 27, 28, 29, 30 December, and what absolutely isn't.
posts.why: Published early enough for people to plan. This post will get saved by everyone visiting London over Christmas and it costs you almost nothing to make.
posts.cta: Save it now, use it in a fortnight
posts.assets: Text graphics + a few clips

shoots.what: Full photo + video set of ONE flagship flat
shoots.how: Daylight only, curtains open, lights off. Every room from the doorway corner. Then 8-10 video clips of 3-5s: kettle boiling, door opening, bed made, window view, kitchen worktop, shower running, key in lock, sofa.

shoots.what: Founder piece-to-camera — 6 scripted clips
shoots.how: Vertical, eye-level, window light on your face, phone 1m away. 15-25s each. Don't memorise, just talk. Reshoot until it sounds like you.
shoots.feeds: Launch post, HUMAN slot, PROOF responses

shoots.what: One complete turnover, filmed start to finish
shoots.how: 15-20 clips of 3-5s AND one continuous unedited take of a single room. No music, real sound. Unglamorous is the point.

shoots.what: Brand title card + on-screen text template
shoots.how: Not filming — a designed 2s intro card reading LONDON THIS WEEK, plus a lower-third text style. Same every week.

shoots.what: Timed walk: flagship flat → nearest station → the venue
shoots.how: ONE continuous take, no cuts, phone held steady at chest height. Speed up 4x in edit, timer overlay. This is your signature format.

shoots.what: Linen store / stock cupboard
shoots.how: One clip, doors open, count out loud. Show the systems: labels, rotation, spares.

shoots.what: Photo sets for 4 more properties at 4 price points
shoots.how: Same method as F01 but lighter — 12 stills + 4 clips each. Studio / 1-bed / 2-bed / large.

shoots.what: Property set: one large flat shot AS A GROUP SPACE
shoots.how: Table laid for 6, sofa with people on it, kitchen in use. Needs 2-3 friendly humans in frame. Very different from an empty-flat shoot.

shoots.what: Team clips — 6 cleaners/staff, one London recommendation each
shoots.how: Can be voice-only over a clip of the place they recommend if they don't want to be on camera. PAY THEM for their time.

shoots.what: Generic London: tube platform, escalator, black cab, red bus, Thames, terrace street, rain on a window, a kettle, keys
shoots.how: 20-30 clips of 3-5s. Shoot on one 2-hour walk. This is your filler library and you will use it constantly.

shoots.what: Heathrow arrivals, luggage storage, Piccadilly line, an early-opening café
shoots.how: For the 6am-landing post. Genuinely go at 6am — the light and the emptiness are the story.

shoots.what: ExCeL, The O2 / North Greenwich, Wembley Stadium + Wembley Way, Twickenham + the walk from the station
shoots.how: 3-5 clips each. One Saturday covers O2 + ExCeL; a second covers Wembley + Twickenham.

shoots.what: Alexandra Palace, Regent's Park, Trafalgar Square, Hyde Park Corner
shoots.how: For darts, Frieze, Diwali and Winter Wonderland posts.

shoots.what: Waterloo→Twickenham, and North Greenwich→O2, both filmed as one continuous journey
shoots.how: Same signature format as F05. Film the actual train, the actual walk. Timer added in edit.

shoots.what: Sir John Soane's, Wellcome Collection, Hunterian, Foundling, Leighton House, Garden Museum
shoots.how: Check each one's filming policy at the desk first — several restrict it. Exteriors always work.

shoots.what: 5 places to eat within 12 min walk of Wembley Park
shoots.how: Shoot the food, the frontage and the walk. Note real prices.

shoots.what: Pubs that take away fans, the station, the walk, the queue
shoots.how: Best filmed ON a matchday — 8 Nov works. Ask permission inside pubs.

shoots.what: Frieze Sculpture in Regent's Park + Mayfair gallery fronts
shoots.how: Free and public. Must be shot 14-18 Oct — it does not exist after that.

shoots.what: Winter Wonderland: entrances, queues, rides, food, the Hyde Park Corner exit
shoots.how: Go on OPENING WEEKEND (19-22 Nov) so the content runs for the full 46 days. Check their filming rules.

shoots.what: Bonfire night displays + the walk home from one
shoots.how: 5 Nov only. Night footage — brace the phone against something solid.
shoots.feeds: LONDON 3 Nov (shoot 2025 or stock for the 3rd, real for follow-ups)

shoots.what: Ten Christmas markets
shoots.how: One weekend covers most of them. Shoot the crowds and the prices, not just the lights.

shoots.what: Nations Championship weekend at Twickenham, filmed live
shoots.how: 27-29 Nov. Crowds, flags, atmosphere. Post SAME DAY.

shoots.what: Your real cost-per-property breakdown (every line item)
shoots.how: A spreadsheet: cleaning, linen, utilities, wifi, insurance, OTA commission, void allowance, restocking, management, licensing.

shoots.what: Export of every guest review, all platforms, last 12 months
shoots.how: CSV or screenshots. Needed for the monthly review posts and the 'we fixed it' format. Include the bad ones — especially the bad ones.

shoots.what: Your standard management agreement
shoots.how: So the team can write the '6 clauses to check' post honestly against your own contract.

shoots.what: A real hotel comparison — screenshot 3 comparable hotels + your rate, same dates
shoots.how: Must be checkable and dated. Never invent these numbers.

shoots.what: Property list: address, area, nearest station, beds, sleeps, nightly rate, nearest major venue
shoots.how: The single most useful document for the whole team. Without it, every location post is guesswork.

shoots.what: A property you turned down, and why
shoots.how: For the LANDLORD 4 Nov post. Real case, anonymised.

shoots.what: Written permission from one guest to tell their story
shoots.how: Ask a happy long-stay guest. Offer something — a discount on their next stay.

shoots.what: Logo files, brand colours, fonts — or a decision to create them
shoots.how: If these don't exist, that's the first design job. Everything else waits on it.
